title: Involuntary Downgrade Refunds on Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand
content:
**Customer commitment — involuntary downgrades.** A passenger of Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand moved involuntarily to a lower cabin, or off the extra-legroom seating the fare brand includes, on a segment because of an equipment swap or an oversold premium cabin receives a downgrade refund of the fare brand's downgrade compensation percent of that segment's one-way segment fare, paid to the original form of payment, whatever the cause recorded for the disruption. The amount is rounded to the cent.

| Fare brand | Downgrade compensation (percent of the segment fare) |
|---|---|
| Crestline Basic Economy | 0 |
| Crestline Main Cabin | 0 |
| Crestline Main Plus | 20 |
| Crestline Main Flexible | 0 |
| Crestline Premium Economy | 50 |
| Crestline First | 75 |

## Conditions

- A downgrade is compensated only when a disruption record of type involuntary downgrade exists on the segment.
- A fare brand whose downgrade compensation is zero has no cabin or seating entitlement it can be moved below, and receives no downgrade refund.
- A move requested by the passenger is never compensated.

## Alongside the refund

Any seat or upgrade fee paid for the segment is refunded in full under the fee-refund rule in addition to this compensation, and no goodwill is paid for the same disruption.

## Hypothetical worked cases

| Fare brand | Segment fare | Downgrade refund |
|---|---|---|
| Crestline Main Plus | 245.00 | 49.00 |
| Crestline Premium Economy | 386.90 | 193.45 |
| Crestline First | 500.00 | 375.00 |
| Crestline Main Cabin | 300.00 | None |
